bind.createSource: Create the source directory if it is missing
bind.createSourceHint: Created as a dataset when the parent is a ZFS dataset, otherwise as a plain directory.
bind.nameHint: Letters, digits, - and _ (also becomes the systemd unit name).
bind.readOnlyLabel: Read-only (writing through the target is refused)
bind.source: Source — where the data actually lives
bind.sourceHint: For example a ZFS dataset (/mnt/fontos/kz) or a folder inside a mergerfs pool.
bind.target: Target — where users will see it
bind.targetHint: For example /mnt/family_pool/kz/fontos. The directory is created automatically if missing.
binds.deleteConfirm: Delete bind mount "{name}"? Only the presentation goes away; the files on the source are NOT deleted.
binds.empty: No bind mounts yet. A bind mount shows a real directory at a second path, turning physically separate storage into one browsable tree.
binds.intro: A bind mount separates what users browse from where the data actually lives, so "important" on ZFS and "bulk" on a mergerfs pool can appear as two subfolders of a single share.
binds.rootFsWarn: The source is on the system disk, not on a separately mounted filesystem. If you expected ZFS or mergerfs storage here, it is not mounted right now — mount it and save the bind mount again so the boot-order guard is set up correctly.
binds.syncHint: Syncthing and other sync tools: always point them at the REAL source path (e.g. /mnt/fontos/kz), never at the bind target. That way a bind that failed to mount can never make them see an empty folder and propagate deletions.
binds.title: Bind mounts (presentation tree)
binds.unmountConfirm: Unmount bind mount "{name}"? No data is deleted, but the target folder will appear empty in the share.
disks.formatConfirm: WARNING: all data on "{path}" ({size}) will be permanently erased and a new {fstype} filesystem written. Continue?
disks.formatStarted: Formatting started: {path}. This can take a few minutes.
disks.none: No unmounted partitions with a filesystem were found.
disks.noneFormattable: No blank disks or partitions without a filesystem were found.
disks.unmountConfirm: Unmount "{name}" and remove it from fstab? Data is not deleted.
gen.createSourcesHint: Created as datasets under a ZFS dataset, otherwise as plain directories.
gen.foldersHint: Comma separated — usually one per user, e.g. kz, kzs, kv.
gen.hasConflicts: The preview has a conflict — resolve it before creating the tree.
gen.intro: Give the presentation root, the folder names and the tiers — the GUI works out every bind mount needed. For example 3 folder names × 2 tiers = 6 bind mounts.
gen.label: label
gen.previewEmpty: Fill in the root, at least one folder name and at least one tier.
gen.rootHint: The tree is built below this, and this is typically the single path you share. For example /mnt/family_pool.
gen.tiersHint: The subfolder shown under every folder name, and the storage root behind it. E.g. "fontos" → /mnt/fontos (ZFS), "nemfontos" → /mnt/bulk (mergerfs).
gen.title: Generate a tree from a template
policy.eplfs: eplfs — existing path, least free space
policy.epmfs: epmfs — existing path, most free space
policy.mfs: mfs — branch with the most free space
policy.pfrd: pfrd — random, weighted by free space
pool.deleteConfirm: Delete pool "{name}"? Files on the branches are NOT deleted.
pool.extraHint: Comma-separated extra options, e.g. func.getattr=newest. Leave empty if unsure.
pool.minfreeHint: Branches with less free space than this are skipped for new files (e.g. 4G, 250G).
pool.mountpointHint: Where the merged filesystem appears, e.g. /mnt/pool/media.
pool.moveonenospc: Move file to another branch when one runs out of space (moveonenospc)
pool.nameHint: Letters, digits, - and _ (also used as the fsname).
pool.noBranches: Add at least one branch — a mounted disk or any folder.
pools.empty: No pools yet. A pool merges several disks/folders into one big filesystem that you can share.
pools.title: mergerfs pools
sleep.empty: No manageable disks found. The system disk is deliberately hidden here, and only disks with a stable /dev/disk/by-id name can be managed.
sleep.hdIdleBanner: The hd-idle service is running. While it is, it spins disks down too, and the log stays incomplete — the GUI cannot see what it did.
sleep.logEmpty: No log entries match this filter. The log starts filling up once the monitor sees its first state change.
sleep.otherNote: These do not spin, so spinning them down achieves nothing. The Proxmox system disk (and every partition, LVM volume or ZFS vdev on it) does not appear on this page at all.
sleep.settingDefault: Default idle time for new disks
sleep.settingDefaultHint: A newly installed disk starts with this until you change it. “Never” is the safe default.
sleep.settingEnabledHint: When off, the monitor only observes and logs, and never spins anything down. Manual sleep still works.
sleep.settingPollHint: Determines how precise the timeline is. Checking does not wake the disks.
sleep.settingRetentionHint: Older events are removed daily. The database lives on the system disk, so it never wakes a data disk.
sleep.spinDownConfirm: {disk} will be put to sleep now. The next request to it will spin it back up, which takes a few seconds. Continue?
sleep.takeoverConfirm: The hd-idle service will be stopped and disabled, and its settings imported. Continue?
sleep.takeoverDone: hd-idle stopped, settings imported for {count} disk(s).
sleep.title: Disk sleep
sleep.warnCount: {count} thing(s) may keep this disk awake
sleepwarn.mergerfs_cache.body: mergerfs' own documentation says spin-up cannot be reliably prevented at the pool level: mergerfs is a proxy, not a cache, and a directory listing touches every branch by definition. These options only filter out repeated metadata requests.
sleepwarn.mergerfs_cache.title: mergerfs pool “{pool}” runs without metadata caching
sleepwarn.mergerfs_cache.why: Deliberately not applied automatically: it would make a file written directly to a branch, bypassing the pool, visible minutes late.
sleepwarn.noatime.body: The mount currently updates file access times, so reads cause writes to the disk. This is the GUI's own fstab line, so it can be fixed from here.
sleepwarn.noatime.confirm: The fstab line for “{name}” will get the noatime option and the filesystem will be remounted. Continue?
sleepwarn.noatime.title: {mountpoint} is not mounted with noatime
sleepwarn.noatime.why: A backup of fstab is taken the first time it is modified.
sleepwarn.pve_storage.body: pvestatd asks every configured storage for its status every ten seconds; listing the content at {path} touches the disk.
sleepwarn.pve_storage.title: A Proxmox storage (“{id}”) points at this disk
sleepwarn.pve_storage.why: Deliberately not applied automatically: the Proxmox storage config is not this application's to own.
sleepwarn.smartd.body: smartd is running and {path} has a device line with no power-mode guard. Reading SMART data spins a sleeping disk back up — by default every 30 minutes.
sleepwarn.smartd.confirm: The smartd config will get -n standby,q added (a backup is taken first) and smartd will be restarted. Continue?
sleepwarn.smartd.title: smartd wakes this disk regularly
sleepwarn.smartd.why: No SMART data is collected while the disk sleeps; it is picked up at the first check after it wakes.
sleepwarn.updatedb.body: The daily index walks the whole filesystem, waking every disk. Adding the path to PRUNEPATHS in {path} leaves it out of the index.
sleepwarn.updatedb.title: updatedb indexes {mountpoint}
sleepwarn.updatedb.why: Deliberately not applied automatically: {path} belongs to other programs too.
sleepwarn.zfs_atime.body: With atime=on even a read causes a write: the access time of every opened file is written back to disk, so simply browsing the pool wakes it.
sleepwarn.zfs_atime.confirm: This will run: zfs set atime=off {pool}. Continue?
sleepwarn.zfs_atime.title: ZFS pool “{pool}” has atime=on
sleepwarn.zfs_atime.why: Reversible at any time: zfs set atime=on {pool}.
sleepwarn.zfs_autosnapshot.body: A snapshot is a metadata write, so it wakes the disk — the package runs every 15 minutes by default.
sleepwarn.zfs_autosnapshot.title: zfs-auto-snapshot takes snapshots of pool “{pool}”
sleepwarn.zfs_autosnapshot.why: Deliberately not applied automatically: only you know which datasets need snapshots.
sleepwarn.zfs_scrub.body: The Debian package scrubs monthly, which keeps every disk in the pool awake for hours. That is correct behaviour — it is just worth knowing when you see a long stretch of awake time in the log.
sleepwarn.zfs_scrub.title: A scheduled ZFS scrub runs on pool “{pool}”
sleepwarn.zfs_zvol.body: While a running VM or container uses them, the pool's disks keep receiving I/O and will not go to sleep.
sleepwarn.zfs_zvol.title: Pool “{pool}” holds {count} virtual disk(s) (zvol)
